headline: 7 core protocol contracts catalogued across Ethereum (mainnet); 2 additional token-bridge controllers; legacy and current architecture documented.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search identified StarkGate ETH Bridge at 0xae0ee0a63a2ce6baeeffe56e7714fb4efe48d419 on Ethereum mainnet.

Official Starknet docs deployments page lists 7 core StarkGate contracts: StarkgateManager (0x0c5aE94f8939182F2D06097025324D1E537d5B60), StarkgateRegistry (0x1268cc171c54F2000402DfF20E93E60DF4c96812), L1 StarknetTokenBridge (0xF5b6Ee2CAEb6769659f6C091D209DfdCaF3F69Eb), L2 StarknetTokenBridge (0x0616757a151c21f9be8775098d591c2807316d992bbc3bb1a5c1821630589256), plus legacy bridge contracts for backward compatibility with pre-2.0 token bridges.
No formal audit links provided in protocol context; documentation references ABDK and Nethermind audit completions mentioned in StarkGate Alpha blog post but no PDF links provided.

GitHub repository starknet-io/starkgate-contracts contains Solidity (L1) and Cairo (L2) contract source code organized under src/solidity/ and src/cairo/ directories; legacy contract implementations referenced via commit-pinned branches (cairo-1).
Protocol operates on Ethereum mainnet only per pinned protocol.chains=[Ethereum]; Sepolia testnet addresses documented in official docs but not part of pinned assessment scope.
StarkGate Registry and Manager enable dynamic token enrollment; bridged tokens not enumerated in this discovery phase due to factory-pattern scope limits.
Identified role taxonomy: StarkgateManager (manager/factory), StarkgateRegistry (registry), L1/L2 StarknetTokenBridge (core bridge), legacy bridge contracts for backward compatibility.
All admin_addresses entries derive from fetched docs (docs.starknet.io) and verified Etherscan results; no unvetted snippet-only sightings.

protocol_metadata.about: StarkGate is the official canonical bridge developed by StarkWare for transferring ETH and ERC-20 tokens between Ethereum and Starknet. The bridge enables deposits from Ethereum to Starknet (with optional message callbacks) and withdrawals from Starknet back to Ethereum through a dual-contract architecture with L1 and L2 bridge components communicating via Starknet's messaging system. StarkGate 2.0, deployed in January 2024, unified token bridging under a multi-bridge architecture supporting dynamic token enrollment while maintaining backward compatibility with legacy single-token bridges.
